text: And we start well, this can be modeled, as a queue where packets coming from the higher layers get in. And then this queue is works according to the FIFO policy, first input first output. So the first one that arrives gets served, right? So packets may be queued in in the same order as they arrive. And then they they get served one at a time. And this is the server that applies the rules, of the BCF, bunch. That's something that we already knew. And we also knew that when the server services a packet, so it means that it tries to get this packet through and send it to the physical layer, so that the packet can then be transmitted over the wireless channel. Well, it has to follow the rules of the protocol. And the protocol, the MAC protocol, the BCF works using certain parameters, right? The the cves, the leaves, the bives, the extended IFS. The the cough procedure, we all know that. And the cough makes use of the contention window minimum, the contention window maximum. We all know that. Okay. Now, in the announced version of this, what we have is within the same Wi-Fi card. So the same Wi-Fi card does not have only one queue. It has got four queues. That are called access category zero, access category one, access category two, access category three.
